title: DOM events, custom events, bubbling, composition, and Lightning Message Service
objectives: Dispatch a CustomEvent from a child so a parent handles it with an on* listener in the parent template.
Name events in lowercase with underscores, never with an on prefix, and put only primitives or copies in detail.
Choose properties and methods to communicate down, events to communicate up, and Lightning Message Service to communicate across the DOM.
State that LMS can connect LWC, Aura, Visualforce, and utility bar on a Lightning page.
diagnostic_question: A child selection must update a parent, a utility-bar widget must hear the same fact, and a teammate wants to fire an onselected event whose detail is the live contact object. Which DOM event, custom event, bubbling, composition, and Lightning Message Service choices do you make?
definition: Lightning web components dispatch standard DOM events and CustomEvent instances to communicate up the containment hierarchy. Parents listen with on* attributes. Communicate down with public properties or methods. Communicate across the DOM—including Aura, Visualforce, and utility bar—with Lightning Message Service. ([Events](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/events.html); [Create and Dispatch Events](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/events-create-dispatch.html); [LMS](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/use-message-channel.html))
why_it_matters: Interviewers fail candidates who shout down with events, pass mutable objects in detail, name events onselected, or use LMS for a direct parent/child pair. The wrong channel creates hidden coupling and security-sensitive mutation.
sixty_second_explanation: The child does not shout down the stairwell; the parent already passed tickets (@api). The child shouts up with a CustomEvent the parent hears as onselected. Put a contact Id in detail, not the live object. If a Visualforce page or utility bar must hear it too, that is the building PA: Lightning Message Service on a message channel—not another nested event.
deeper_explanation: Use events to communicate up. A child such as c-todo-item dispatches so the parent c-todo-app knows a user selected it. Events are built on DOM Events. Strongly prefer CustomEvent. To communicate down, pass properties or call public methods. To communicate between components that are not in that tree, use Lightning message service or a pub-sub utility. ([Communicate with Events](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/events.html))

Create events with new CustomEvent(type) and dispatch with this.dispatchEvent. Event type strings should have no uppercase, no spaces, and use underscores to separate words. Do not prefix with on, or the parent listener becomes ononmessage. Simple events may have no payload. To pass data, set detail to primitives, or copy objects so listeners cannot mutate your data. ([Create and Dispatch Events](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/events-create-dispatch.html))

Parents listen with HTML attributes oneventtype, for example onprevious and onnext on a nested paginator, or onselected when the child dispatches selected. The parent handler reads event.detail. ([Create and Dispatch Events](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/events-create-dispatch.html))

Lightning Message Service communicates across the DOM on a Lightning page among Visualforce, Aura, and LWC, including utility bar and pop-out utilities. It is available in Lightning Experience and for Lightning components in Experience Builder sites. Choose application-wide versus active-area subscription when you configure scope. ([LMS](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/use-message-channel.html))

mental_model.analogy: A stairwell versus a building PA: the child shouts up with CustomEvent; the parent does not shout down (it passes tickets). Unrelated rooms—Aura, Visualforce, utility bar—use the PA (Lightning Message Service) on a message channel.
useful_mapping: CustomEvent type selected → shout name, lowercase with underscores
parent onselected={handler} → ear on the child's door
detail primitive Id → a slip of paper, not the whole filing cabinet
VF / Aura / utility bar → other rooms on the same floor
where_it_breaks: bubbles and composed flags are DOM mechanics, not acoustics—reverify the propagate page before quoting defaults.
LMS is not a replacement for a direct parent listener.
Pub-sub utilities are mentioned as an alternative but are not the first-party LMS channel.
The analogy does not encode Experience Cloud licensing.

teach_back_prompt: Walk a parent/child selection: the CustomEvent name, the parent on* listener, what belongs in detail, and when you would add Lightning Message Service instead of another nested event.

terminology.plain: The recommended object a component dispatches to announce something happened.
terminology.precise: new CustomEvent(type, { detail }) then this.dispatchEvent. Preferred over ad-hoc event types for a consistent browser experience.
terminology.non_example: Setting a parent field directly from the child.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Aura application events, a different event model.
terminology.boundary: Platform events are integration, not LWC DOM events.

terminology.plain: The string name of the event, such as selected or next.
terminology.precise: No uppercase, no spaces, underscores to separate words. Do not prefix with on.
terminology.non_example: onselected as the type, which forces ononselected in markup.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: HTML onclick, which is a standard DOM listener name, not your custom type.
terminology.boundary: LMS channel names are metadata, not CustomEvent types.

terminology.precise: No required shape, but send primitives or a copy. Passing a live object lets listeners mutate it by reference.
terminology.non_example: detail: this.contact where this.contact is the wired object.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: @api property, which is down, not up.
terminology.boundary: Do not put secrets in detail.

terminology.plain: The parent template attribute that hears the child's event.
terminology.precise: Syntax oneventtype. Event previous → onprevious. Handler receives the event object.
terminology.non_example: window.addEventListener as the first choice for a direct child.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: LMS subscribe, which is not a template on* attribute.
terminology.boundary: Standard lightning-button onclick is a base-component event, still handled with on*.

terminology.plain: Child tells parent via an event.
terminology.precise: Official direction for events in the containment hierarchy.
terminology.example: c-todo-item dispatches so c-todo-app knows it was selected.
terminology.non_example: Parent dispatching an event for the child to set a property.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Bubbling to grandparents, which needs propagate flags—Needs verification.

terminology.plain: The platform PA that carries messages across the page DOM.
terminology.precise: Communicate among VF, Aura, and LWC including utility bar and pop-out utilities. LEX and Experience Builder sites. Subscribe to the whole app or the active area.
terminology.example: Record-page LWC publishes a channel the utility-bar LWC subscribes to.
terminology.non_example: A CustomEvent for a nested child in the same template.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Platform Events / Pub/Sub API, which are org integration, not page DOM.
terminology.boundary: Open CTI softphones are mentioned as an LMS consumer; details are out of scope.

terminology.plain: The named pipe LMS publishers and subscribers share.
terminology.precise: Created as metadata (LightningMessageChannel). Components publish and subscribe on that channel.
terminology.example: LAB_RecordSelected__c message channel used by two LWCs on one page.
terminology.non_example: A CustomEvent type string reused as if it were LMS.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Platform event entity, a different metadata type.
terminology.boundary: Exact XML fields of the channel Need verification on Create a Message Channel.

terminology.plain: DOM flags that decide whether an event climbs ancestors and whether it crosses shadow boundaries.
terminology.precise: Important for grandparents and shadow. Parent on* on the child tag is shown in the dispatch topic without requiring you to invent defaults. Quote bubbles/composed only from the propagate page.
terminology.example: Needs verification: opening Configure Event Propagation before stating default false/false.
terminology.non_example: Using LMS because you are unsure about bubbles.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: LWC composition (parent nesting children), a different word.
terminology.boundary: This lesson flags the topic; it does not invent the table.

when_to_use: When a child Lightning web component must notify its parent with a custom event the parent handles in the template.
When you must choose events for communicating up versus public properties for composition down.
When bubbling beyond the parent or crossing shadow needs the official propagate page rather than invented flags.
When Visualforce, Aura, or a utility bar must hear a message: Lightning Message Service, not a nested CustomEvent.
When detail on a custom event should be a primitive or a copy, not a live wired object.
when_not_to_use: Do not use custom events to push data down into a child—that is @api composition (LWC-004).
Do not use Lightning Message Service as the default for a parent that already nests the child in its template.
Do not treat this events lesson as LDS/Apex data access (LWC-006).
Do not invent bubbles/composed defaults without the propagate page.
Do not publish LMS messages with real customer secrets from a lab org.

interview_questions.question: How do Lightning web components communicate up, down, and across?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Up: CustomEvent to the parent. Down: @api properties or methods. Across the DOM, including Aura, Visualforce, and utility bar: Lightning Message Service.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I start from the Events tip. I do not fire events downward. I do not use LMS for a nested child. I name events without an on prefix. I keep detail primitive. I refuse to invent bubbles defaults.
interview_questions.example: c-lab-item dispatches selected with an Id; parent onselected; utility bar uses LMS.

interview_questions.question: How do you create and listen for a custom event?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: In the child, new CustomEvent('selected', { detail: id }) and dispatchEvent. In the parent template, onselected={handler} and read event.detail.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I show paginator previous/next with no payload and the contact-list selected Id. I stress lowercase underscore names. I copy objects if I must send more than an Id. I import nothing extra for CustomEvent; it is a browser API.
interview_questions.example: labPaginator onprevious/onnext changing pageNumber in the parent class.
tradeoffs: One event vs two types previous/next
follow_ups: Why two event types on the paginator?

interview_questions.question: A teammate puts the whole wired contact in detail. What do you change?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Pass the Id or a copied plain object. Live objects are by reference; the parent could mutate the child's data.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I cite Create and Dispatch Events. The parent already has the contacts array from @wire or a list; it looks up by Id like the recipes component. I also strip fields the listener should not see. I do not switch to LMS just because detail was wrong.
interview_questions.example: detail: this.contact.Id instead of detail: this.contact from a wired list item.
tradeoffs: Extra parent logic vs safer child
follow_ups: What if the parent does not have the list?
weak_answer_warnings: Passing the proxy object because it is convenient

interview_questions.question: Visualforce on the same Lightning page must react to an LWC button. CustomEvent or LMS?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Lightning Message Service. CustomEvent stays in the LWC containment tree and is not the VF bridge.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: LMS is documented for VF, Aura, and LWC including utility bar. I create a message channel and publish/subscribe. I pick application versus active-area scope from the LMS pages. I do not invent a DOM bubble into iframe VF without that service.
interview_questions.example: LWC publishes LAB_RecordSelected__c; a VF page on the same record page subscribes.
tradeoffs: LMS vs replacing VF with LWC
weak_answer_warnings: window.postMessage as the first official answer

interview_questions.question: Parent wrote onselected but nothing runs. The child type is onselected. What is wrong?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The type should be selected. onselected as the type makes the listener ononselected. Rename the CustomEvent type.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I also check dispatchEvent is reached, the handler is bound with {handleSelected}, and the listener sits on the child tag. I do not flip bubbles as the first fix. I look at spelling of underscores.
follow_ups: What if the type has a space?

interview_questions.question: A grandparent never sees the child's event. What do you not invent?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I do not invent bubbles and composed defaults. I open Configure Event Propagation. Meanwhile I can have the parent re-dispatch or pass a callback property if the design allows.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: This pack marks propagate defaults as Needs verification. Interview honesty beats a memorized false/false. If the listener is on the child tag in the parent, the dispatch topic already shows that working. Grandparent and shadow crossing are the propagate page.
interview_questions.example: Parent listens onselected on c-lab-item; grandparent needs its own listener or a re-dispatch from the parent.
tradeoffs: Read the propagate page vs guess
follow_ups: What does composed mean in DOM terms?
Is a container guaranteed to hear all events?
weak_answer_warnings: Stating unverified default booleans as fact

interview_questions.question: When would you skip both CustomEvent and LMS?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the parent can pass a property or call an @api method, or when a base component event already exists, or when no UI communication is needed because the server owns the state.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Not every click needs a custom type. lightning-button onclick may be enough inside one component. Parent-to-child reset is an @api method (LWC-004). Record refresh after Apex is LWC-006. I add LMS only when another DOM tree must hear it.
interview_questions.example: A child's internal toggle stays private; only commit dispatches selected.
tradeoffs: Internal state vs public event contract
follow_ups: When is a platform event the real tool?

interview_questions.question: Teach this with the stairwell versus PA analogy and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Child shouts up the stairwell with CustomEvent; parent does not shout down. Other rooms use the building PA (LMS). It breaks on bubbles/composed flags and on licensing for Experience Cloud.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I draw the parent/child mermaid: properties down, selected up, LMS to utility bar and VF. I name events correctly and keep detail primitive. I never use a generic catalog metaphor. I admit the propagate page was not inlined here.
interview_questions.example: labContactItem selected Id, parent onselected, utility bar LMS subscriber.
follow_ups: How does composition mean two different things?
